meta.source: Renewables.ninja / MERRA-2. Wind: Vestas V90 2000 at 80m. PV: tilt=|latitude|, equator-facing, 10% system loss. Same configuration and coordinates as profiles_regional.json, so the years are directly comparable.
meta.purpose: Inter-annual weather variability. South Africa has the most variable solar resource in Africa (CV ~0.4, ENSO/IOD driven), so single-year results understate risk.
meta.encoding: Series are integers scaled by "scale" (1000): divide by 1000 for per-unit output. The source data is 3dp, so this is lossless and cuts the file from 9.0 MB to 5.4 MB - it was two-thirds of the whole site payload.

meta.wind_rebuilt: MULTI-SITE, 6 Sep 2026. Capacity-weighted mean of up to 12 sites per region from Renewables.ninja MERRA-2. Replaces one centroid per region, which sat below 2% output 60 h/yr against Eskom-observed 7. Sites from REEA permits, REDZ where permits are thin, province spread where neither - see profile_sites.json basis.
meta.solar_note: UNCHANGED. The multi-site pull reproduces the MERRA-2 50 km compression PVGIS was adopted to fix. Years 2024, 2025 added 6 Sep 2026 at the SAME single centroids as 2014-2023, not multi-site, so the sampling method is consistent across every year. meta.bias_corrected: 6 Sep 2026. Wind scaled by 1.0753 so the capacity-weighted national mean matches Eskom observation over 2022-2023.
meta.correction_warning: This file is CALIBRATED. Its level matches observation by construction, so a check comparing its mean CF against Eskom no longer tests the underlying method - only the arithmetic. The SHAPE is uncalibrated and remains a real test: calm-hour counts were 2.1x observed at the 5% threshold before this.
meta.solar_source: PVGIS PVGIS-SARAH3 at 5 km, aspect=180, tilt=|latitude|, 10% system loss. Replaces MERRA-2 at 50 km, which compressed the regional spread to 1.07x against a real 1.4-1.5x. Rebuilt 6 Sep 2026. Regional spread now 1.24x.
meta.solar_borrowed_years: 20 region-years outside PVGIS coverage (2005-2020) keep their own MERRA-2 hourly timing, rescaled to the 2023 PVGIS regional level. The geography is corrected; the weather is not measured. Solar varies 3.3% between years so this is a small compromise, but it is a compromise.
meta.solar_timezone: SHIFTED +2 h from UTC to SAST on 8 Sep 2026. PVGIS returns UTC and has no timezone parameter, while wind is fetched from Renewables.ninja with local_time=true - so the two carriers sat on different clocks in this file. Size confirmed two ways at the profile centroid: solar noon at 21.073E is 12:27-12:43 SAST (hour 12, PVGIS gave hour 10), and the daylight WINDOW lengths already matched at 10/12/14 hours, so it was displaced not distorted. Any future PVGIS pull must apply the same shift.
